recommendation_1: Reduce mid_dim from 100 to 32 to drastically decrease the number of trainable parameters and memory footprint.
rationale_1: Lowering the hidden dimension directly reduces the size of weight matrices and activations, which significantly decreases both RAM usage and computational energy consumption without compromising performance on MNIST.
recommendation_4: Switch to Bfloat16 Autocast during training and inference to reduce memory usage and improve numerical stability on CPU hardware.
rationale_4: Using BF16 precision halves the memory footprint per parameter compared to FP32, allowing larger models to fit within limited RAM constraints and reducing power consumption.
recommendation_5: Replace ReLU activations with Swish (SiLU) activation functions to potentially improve convergence speed and reduce energy consumption due to more efficient gradient flow.
rationale_5: Swish activation can lead to faster training and lower final loss, indirectly improving energy efficiency through reduced training time and better generalization on skewed datasets like MNIST.
recommendation_6: Remove the second linear layer (fc2) and simplify the architecture to a single hidden layer with reduced mid_dim=32 to further minimize memory and computational overhead.
rationale_6: Eliminating one linear layer reduces the total number of parameters and operations, which lowers memory usage and energy consumption while still achieving acceptable performance on MNIST.
